items.summary: A feature-provider version (silver_v5) that assembles the fundamentals inputs the live categories read from point-in-time history instead of the yfinance snapshot
added: A feature-provider version builds the fundamentals inputs of the composite categories from point-in-time statement history — annual statements (FY2020+) and quarterly key figures with balance-sheet lines (2017+) — using each row's published_at as the visibility boundary at the step's decision instant. A row published after the step is invisible; an input with no point-in-time source stays absent, never zero and never back-filled from a later snapshot.

Derived inputs (price multiples, leverage, liquidity, margin, growth and cash-flow measures) follow the same definitions the live categories use, and each carries the as-of date of its oldest component. The mapping from live input to history column, including inputs declared absent, is written down with the change before the provider ships.

The replay manifest reports per-category non-null coverage per step. The promotion test reads that coverage and returns window-not-evaluable when non-technical coverage is below its floor; it never grades a window the provider could not populate.
Parity covers the fundamentals categories on any window where both the live snapshot source and the history provider exist, with a stated agreement target; a miss names the category.

items.title: Backtests now include trading costs
items.headline: Simulated trades now pay spreads, broker fees and market impact, and results are shown before and after costs, so strategies aren't judged on flattering gross returns.
items.summary: A cost model inside replay, applied to every fill and reported separately
added: Every replayed fill pays an explicit cost: a half-spread by liquidity bucket (market capitalisation and median daily turnover), a commission per order from the Avanza and Nordnet stock courtage tiers (Savr is fund-only, out of scope), and an impact term proportional to the order's share of median daily turnover above a stated threshold. The parameters are part of the policy (costs block); a comparison of two policies is rejected unless both carry the same block.
NAV, total return and drawdown are reported both gross and net of costs; the promotion test judges the NAV criterion on the net series. Rank IC is unchanged by costs.
The manifest records the cost block and the realised cost drag in basis points of traded notional; a comparison prints both arms' drag next to their returns.

Spread estimates per bucket come from a dated calibration file that states the method, the estimates and their sample sizes; it changes only through a proposal. Where no quote data exists the estimate is a bounded proxy that errs toward overstating cost.

items.title: Quarterly reported vs adjusted profit collected
items.headline: The app now gathers each quarterly report's reported and adjusted operating profit, so it can tell which companies keep excluding one-off costs.
items.summary: A sibling extraction, investor.data_lake.report_adjusted_profit, with the same release list, page fetch, body matching, retry rules and usage-meter chunking as report_key_figures but its own prompt and bronze log (so the key-figure extractor's accuracy test stays valid)
added: The lake SHALL hold a silver report_adjusted_profit table with one row per MFN interim-report release in silver report_events that has an error-free extraction. Each row carries instrument_id, published_at, session_date, period, the quarter's as-published reported_msek and adjusted_msek operating profit, the profit level both are stated at (family: EBIT, EBITA or EBITDA), whether the release presents an adjusted measure at all (has_adjusted_measure), and the extraction model and prompt version.

The adjusted and reported figures of a row SHALL be at the same profit level. EBIT SHALL be preferred, then EBITA, then EBITDA; an adjusted EBITA SHALL never be paired with a reported EBIT. Half-year, nine-month, full-year and prior-year figures SHALL never stand in for the quarter's own.
The as-of time of a row SHALL be its published_at.

The extraction SHALL keep its own bronze log and prompt version, separate from report_key_figures, with the same resumable, bounded, usage-paced backfill rules (a logged release is not re-fetched; a body-less page or unparseable answer is final; a transient failure is retried).

items.title: Years of insider and short-selling history added
items.headline: Insider trades back to 2016 and short positions back to 2012 are now loaded, so these signals can be tested on a long record instead of a few months.
items.summary: Silver short_positions starts 2026-06-18 and insider_events 2025-09-10, so the short-interest and insider shadow signals (spikes S09, S10) can only be tested on months of data and the insider_pbook_conviction component has no history
added: Insider transactions published by Finansinspektionen from the start of MAR reporting (2016-07-03) to the first daily capture are back-filled per issuer into bronze (keyed by issuer and year, bounded per run, resumable) and imported into silver insider_events with the live importer's fields and a source_basis of fi_history.
The lake coverage report states, for short_positions and insider_events, the earliest date present and the share of historical rows that resolved to an instrument, by year.

The full public history of significant net short positions published by Finansinspektionen (from the register's start in 2012) is captured once from FI's historical file and re-captured when the file changes; the capture is keyed by file date and kept in bronze.

Historical rows are imported into the silver short_positions table with the same fields as daily captures and a source_basis of fi_history, so a reader can distinguish back-filled history from live snapshots. ISINs that do not resolve to an instrument are reported by year in the lake coverage report, never dropped silently.

items.title: Annual balance sheets from 2020 added
items.headline: The app now collects companies' annual financial statements from free public filings, dated to when they became public, giving a longer history for fundamentals.
items.summary: A bronze source and a silver table for annual IFRS statements
added: Bronze source esef_filings captures, once per (LEI, period_end), the metadata of an ESEF annual-report filing published by the filings.xbrl.org repository together with its non-dimensional facts (concept, period, unit, value). Dimensional (segment) facts are not captured. Discovery is limited to filings whose entity LEI belongs to a universe issuer; the LEI comes from the issuer's MFN archive and is reported as unresolved, never guessed, when absent. A captured key is never re-fetched; a run is bounded and resumable.

Silver table annual_statements holds one row per (instrument_id, fiscal_year) with: period_end, published_at, published_at_basis (mfn_annual_release | statutory_lag), currency, source (esef), and the statement lines revenue, operating_profit, profit_loss, total_assets, equity, total_liabilities, current_assets, current_liabilities, noncurrent_liabilities, cash, cfo, capex_ppe, capex_intangibles, dividends_paid, depreciation_amortisation. A line the filing does not tag is null; no line is ever derived from another except total_liabilities = EquityAndLiabilities − Equity when Liabilities is absent, and that derivation is flagged in a derived list on the row.

Concept fallbacks are fixed and ordered: revenue Revenue → RevenueFromContractsWithCustomers; equity EquityAttributableToOwnersOfParent → Equity; profit ProfitLoss; operating profit ProfitLossFromOperatingActivities; cash flow from operations CashFlowsFromUsedInOperatingActivities; capex PurchaseOfPropertyPlantAndEquipmentClassifiedAsInvestingActivities and PurchaseOfIntangibleAssetsClassifiedAsInvestingActivities; dividends DividendsPaidClassifiedAsFinancingActivities. Instant facts are read at the filing's period end; duration facts must span exactly the fiscal year ending at that period end. The fiscal year end is read from the filing, never assumed to be December.

published_at is the point-in-time boundary for every reader: the MFN annual-report release for that fiscal year when one exists in report_events, otherwise period_end + 120 days with basis statutory_lag. The repository's own date_added is never used as a publication date.

items.title: Owner-count signal now reads rising owners as positive
items.headline: By your decision, a growing number of owners in a stock now counts as a positive signal rather than a negative one.
items.summary: Set the default direction to +1.0

items.title: Quarterly balance-sheet figures collected since 2017
items.headline: The app now reads equity, net debt, cash, cash flow and total assets from quarterly reports, each dated to when it was published, after an accuracy check.
items.summary: Extend the existing MFN key-figure extraction (same release pages, same extraction log, same never-re-fetch rule, same usage-meter bounding) with five balance-sheet and cash-flow lines per interim release: equity, net_debt (as published, or null when the issuer does not state it), cash, cfo_period (operating cash flow
added: The point-in-time quarterly key figures read from MFN interim-report releases also carry, per release: equity, net_debt, cash, cfo_period with a cfo_is_ytd flag, and total_assets, each as published on the release page and null when the page does not state it. They share the release's published_at as their as-of time and are never restated.

Every extracted row records the extraction_version that produced its lines, so a later pass that adds lines re-reads a release at most once per version and never re-extracts lines an earlier version already produced.

A new or changed extractor is qualified before any back-fill by a pre-registered accuracy test on a fixed, hand-labelled set of reports with a stated exact-match threshold per line; the result and every miss are recorded with the change. A failing test blocks the back-fill.
Year-to-date cash-flow statements are stored as published and flagged; a reader derives a single quarter only by differencing two flagged values from the same fiscal year.

items.title: New Research page on the dashboard
items.headline: The dashboard now has a Research page showing ongoing experiments, how past changes performed, how trustworthy the backtests are, and what's planned next.
items.summary: Add a Research view to the published dashboard, fed by new sections of the web export
added: The published dashboard has a Research view showing the learning loop's state: research spikes, the change-outcome ledger, backtest honesty, data-watch items and the backlog.
The spike board lists every spike with state, class, priority, verdict, concluded date and a one-line result, and shows the concluded and kill-share counts for the trailing 28 days.

The change ledger lists recently archived changes with the predicted metric and direction, the measured 7-day and 28-day outcome and a verdict of confirmed, contradicted or unmeasured, with per-class hit rates and the classes currently demoted.

The backtest honesty panel states, for the champion replay window, the coverage of each scoring category, the survivorship status, whether net-of-cost results exist and the earliest date of point-in-time fundamentals. Absent inputs read "unmeasured", never zero.

items.title: Weekly automatic documentation upkeep
items.headline: A weekly automated review keeps the project's documentation accurate and well organised, and fixes small mismatches between the documentation and how the app works.
items.summary: A weekly autonomous docs steward (investor.project_setup.docs_steward, investor-docs-steward.{service,timer}) that walks the whole repository and leaves documentation, requirements and specs true and readable, with permission to make small
added: A docs-steward loop runs at most once per 6.5 days (its timer fires daily so a skipped slot is retried the next day) and maintains documentation, requirements and specs across the whole repository against the layout and writing rules in openspec/orchestration/documentation-standard.md.

The documentation is a tree: a one-screen README.md, a documentation hub at docs/README.md linking each branch (requirements, capabilities, operations, data, decisions, guides), and one-topic leaf pages, each reachable from exactly one parent overview.

Every capability spec carries a living body — ## Capability (plain language: what, for whom, which targets, where the code lives) and ## Requirements (current state, consolidated, stable ###  headings) — above its archived delta history. Consolidation never changes a requirement's meaning; a doc/code disagreement is resolved by fixing the doc, making a small local code fix with a test, or opening a proposal.
The loop may change code only for small, local fixes that bring code in line with an unambiguous requirement; any behavior change is a proposal.

items.title: Large code clean-ups handed to the engineer
items.headline: When a code tidy-up is too big for one automated pass, it's written up as a proposal for the engineer instead of being attempted directly.
items.summary: refactor-loop (archived 2026-10-17) makes one small refactor per pass from a size-ranked hotspot list
added: The refactor loop's structural target is openspec/architecture/code-principles.md, which the loop reads and may not edit.

A refactor that does not fit one reviewed pass is not attempted in code. The loop instead writes an OpenSpec proposal marked Origin: refactor-loop stating the current shape, the target shape, the stable public surface, and ordered tasks of one engineer pass each; the product engineer implements it from its normal backlog.
A pass whose code diff exceeds the per-pass cap (changed lines with renames excluded) is not pushed as code; the loop is directed to revert it and write the proposal instead.

The loop may create new change folders but may not edit existing proposals, IDEAS.md, or archived changes. A new proposal must carry the origin marker, pass the strict OpenSpec check, contain no unfilled template placeholders, and keep open refactor-originated proposals at or below two.

items.title: Time-boxed research experiments with preset pass rules
items.headline: New ideas can now be tested in short experiments, with the success and failure rules written down before the first run, so results stay honest.
items.summary: A research-spike capability: one markdown file per spike under openspec/spikes/, with a frontmatter header (id, state, class, objective, opened, priority, verdict) and six required sections — Hypothesis, Pre-registered test, Kill rule, Continue rule, Data, Result log
added: A research spike is one file at openspec/spikes/<id>.md whose id equals the filename stem. Its frontmatter carries state (ready, running, concluded), class (engine, signal, measurement, loop, data), objective (the health-metric key the verdict is judged against), opened, priority, and — only when concluded — verdict (kill, continue, promote) and concluded.

Every spike has six sections: Hypothesis, Pre-registered test, Kill rule, Continue rule, Data, Result log. The kill and continue rules are written before the first run and are not loosened afterwards; a test that cannot run as written is recorded as a blocker, not re-specified.
A spike tests only data that exists on the day it is opened. Work that needs future data is a data proposal or a DATA_WATCH entry, not a spike.
A spike may test anything, including replacing the engine, the horizon or the evaluation ruler; it is not limited to adding a scoring category.

items.title: Tracking whether each change really helped
items.headline: Every change now logs the improvement it predicted, and the result is checked after 7 and 28 days, showing which kinds of changes actually work.
items.summary: Three weeks of uninterrupted autonomous operation produced 165 engineer iterations and 101 audits, yet the metrics that define "the system got better at investing" did not move: 0 replay runs and 0 challengers evaluated in the trailing 7 days, 0 challengers promoted all-time, 0 categories graduated in 90 days, and HIGH
added: Every archived change leaves a prediction row in an append-only ledger (data/change_outcomes.jsonl): the targets and health-metric keys its ## Product contribution names, an expected direction per metric (+1 / −1 / 0 when unparseable, with the sentence kept verbatim), the metric values from the latest health snapshot at archive time, and the capabilities its spec deltas touch (its work class).

Each real health snapshot back-fills the 7-day and 28-day readings for rows whose window has elapsed and judges predicted direction at 28 days. A window already measured is never overwritten: the first reading after the window elapses is the one that counts.
The ledger never blocks an archive or a snapshot; failure to record is reported in the archive message, not raised.

Health: t14_change_outcomes_measured_share_28d — share of archives ≥ 28 days old carrying a 28-day reading (target ≥ 90%, UNMEASURED until the first row is 28 days old); its detail carries the predicted-direction hit rate (T14).

items.title: Automatic nightly code tidy-up
items.headline: A scheduled routine now tidies the code every night without changing behaviour, and only keeps changes that pass all tests and an independent review.
items.summary: Add a dedicated loop, investor.daily_iteration.refactor_loop, run by investor-refactor.timer at 04:30 daily (off the 4h Claude-slot grid by owner decision; window guard + usage meter still price the slot)
added: A scheduled refactor loop (investor.daily_iteration.refactor_loop, role document openspec/agents/refactor-engineer.md) performs behavior-preserving structural changes across src/, tests/, scripts/ and web/: splitting oversized modules, moving top-level modules into their capability package behind a shim, retiring unused shims, and removing duplication. It never changes behavior, specs, proposals, product.md, configuration, data, or systemd units.

Its write scope is enforced by the runner: any path outside src/, tests/, scripts/, web/, docs/context/ and openspec/orchestration/refactor-log.md, or any change to the safety gate or its tests, aborts the run as a write-scope MISS with nothing pushed.

Before review, the runner itself runs ruff, mypy, the full pytest suite, and a format check on touched Python files, and rejects a pass whose collected test count is lower than the run's baseline. One repair attempt is allowed; a pass still failing is reverted and not pushed.
Every pushed pass clears the deterministic safety gate and the independent reviewer, and is committed under the loop's own git identity (refactor), which counts as loop-authored for T9.

items.title: Earnings dates refreshed once they have passed
items.headline: Report dates that are already in the past are now looked up again, so the earnings calendar moves on to each company's next report.
items.summary: investor.earnings_calendar also re-fetches an entry whose cached report date is more than post_days days in the past, both in refresh_batch and in the get_earnings_date cache check
added: The earnings-calendar cache SHALL re-fetch an entry whose cached earnings date is more than earnings_blackout.post_days days in the past, even when its 7-day TTL has not run out. This applies to both the daily refresh and the per-ticker lookup. An entry whose date is within the post-earnings cool-off SHALL keep that date, so the blackout gate's cool-off check still sees it.

items.title: Backtests can use trailing-year earnings and margins
items.headline: Past-period tests now compute price-to-earnings and operating margin from the last four published quarters, only for dates when those reports were public.
items.summary: The backtest's evidence line reads graham (h=1, t=−2.76) and valuation (h=1, t=−2.63) as negative over 8 weeks
added: The lake can give a point-in-time trailing-twelve-month (TTM) reading of net sales, operating profit (EBIT) and EPS for an instrument. Each is the sum of the four latest interim releases in silver report_key_figures published by the as-of time. The TTM operating margin is TTM EBIT over TTM net sales.

A TTM reading is absent, never estimated, in these cases: fewer than four quarterly releases are knowable, or the latest is more than 200 days old. It is also absent when the four latest do not cover each calendar quarter exactly once, or when they span more than 400 days. A TTM field is absent unless all four quarters state it. The operating margin is absent without positive TTM net sales. Swedish and English copies of one report count as one release.

A replay policy can score valuation and margin inputs over history from as-published interim key figures. A policy that pins the silver_v4 feature provider gets everything silver_v3 gives, and two more inputs at each step's decision instant. The first is the trailing P/E: the step's close over the trailing-twelve-month EPS. It is used only where no fundamentals snapshot states a P/E, because the snapshot wins where it exists, as live. The second is the trailing-twelve-month operating margin, from the same table. Silver fundamentals snapshots carry no margin, so the replayed margin always comes from key figures, also after 2026-07, where live reads the provider's margin instead. Parity on this input is approximate, not exact.

A replayed trailing P/E is absent when TTM EPS is absent or not positive, and when the ratio exceeds 200. A ratio that high comes from EPS near zero, or from a figure reported in another currency than the SEK share price.

items.title: Backtests can now judge growth over history
items.headline: Past-period tests now use revenue and earnings growth from quarterly reports as they were published, so growth signals can be checked against history.
items.summary: Replay cannot judge any fundamentals category over history
added: A replay policy can score growth over history from as-published interim key figures. A policy that pins the silver_v3 feature provider gets, for each instrument and step, the revenue growth and earnings growth of the latest interim report published by the step's decision instant, compared with the same quarter a year earlier (net sales and EPS from silver report_key_figures). This is the quarter-over-year-ago basis of the live growth inputs.

A growth input is absent, never guessed, when the latest report is more than 200 days old at the decision instant, when no same-quarter report was published 300 to 430 days before it, when either figure is missing, or when the year-ago figure is not positive. A report published after the decision instant is never used.
silver_v2 policies are unchanged: they read no key figures. A run's manifest records the provider its policy pinned, and silver_v2 and silver_v3 runs both count as live-parity runs.

The replayed growth input carries no fundamental screen, so the live screen's revenue-decline penalty is not replayed and the screen-based quality and safety adjustments stay absent. As in live scoring, the revenue growth input also feeds quality's earnings-quality dimension, so under silver_v3 quality can score for a name with growth data alone. The snapshot ROE stays available to quality when growth inputs are present.

items.title: Quarterly sales, profit and earnings history collected
items.headline: The app now gathers net sales, operating profit and earnings per share from each quarterly report, dated to the release, giving a reliable history for backtests.
items.summary: investor.data_lake.report_key_figures
added: The lake SHALL hold a silver report_key_figures table with one row per MFN interim-report release in silver report_events. Each row carries instrument_id, published_at, session_date, period, the quarter's as-published net_sales_msek, ebit_msek and eps_sek (null when the release does not state the quarter's figure), and the extraction model and prompt version.
The as-of time of a row SHALL be its published_at. A figure SHALL never be read as known before the release that stated it.

Figures SHALL come from the release page text by structured LLM extraction. Operating profit SHALL be the reported EBIT. EBITA and adjusted figures SHALL never stand in for it, and half-year, nine-month or full-year figures SHALL never stand in for the quarter's own.

The backfill SHALL be resumable: each extraction is appended to a bronze log keyed by release id, a release already in the log is not re-fetched, and a run takes a maximum release count. A release whose page has no body or whose answer is unparseable is final and counted; a transient failure (network error, model unavailable or over quota) is logged and retried on a later run.

items.title: Same-day prices settle faster after market close
items.headline: When the final daily price is late, the day's price is now built from intraday data once the market has closed, and replaced by the official figure later.
items.summary: Find out why the 2026-10-13 pulse frames did not settle the 2026-10-12 rows
added: A closed session settles from its intraday bars when the daily row is late. When the provider has not yet published a priced daily row for a closed session, the refresh settles that session's provisional daily bar from the session's own 15m bars. This applies only when the 15m series is complete: it reaches the close and was captured after the close. The bar is marked as intraday-derived, and the provider's settled daily row replaces it once that row is published. A thinly traded name whose 15m series has gaps stays provisional until the daily row arrives.
Intraday bars are not frozen mid-bar. A 15m bar captured while it was still forming is replaced by a later capture taken after the bar closed.

items.title: Stricter evidence bar for changing score weights
items.headline: A signal now counts as proven only if its result holds over at least eight separate weeks. Shorter-lived results are flagged as fragile.
items.summary: format_category_performance (src/investor/engineer.py) counts a row as evidence only when |xs t| >= 2 and cross_sections >= 8
added: The engineer prompt's category-performance evidence verdict SHALL name a category only when its cross-sectional |t| >= 2 rests on at least 8 non-overlapping weeks (cross_sections). Categories that clear |t| >= 2 on fewer weeks SHALL be listed on a separate line as fragile and SHALL NOT count as evidence for a weight or budget change. When only fragile rows clear the bar, the verdict SHALL state that none do.

items.title: Test of giving quality more weight
items.headline: A new check uses real past recommendations to see whether giving company quality more weight would have improved results. It changes nothing live.
items.summary: An evidence-only kill-test, scripts/evaluate_quality_budget_live.py, with the rule below fixed in this proposal before the script produced a number.
added: The quality-budget evidence test evaluates the composite under the quality budget scaled by k ∈ {1.0, 1.5, 2.0} on live decision-audit rows, using composite + (k − 1) × quality per row. Sections are the first audit day of each ISO week with at least 30 names carrying a resolved settled-close forward return.
The test reports, per horizon h ∈ {1, 4} weeks, each arm's mean per-section Spearman rank IC and the mean paired delta against k = 1.0, with the t-stat taken over non-overlapping sections only.

The verdict for k = 2.0 is pre-registered: insufficient below 12 h=1 sections; promotion_candidate when the h=1 mean delta is at least +0.01 with t ≥ 2, the h=4 phase-mean delta is positive, and the h=1 mean delta stays positive after dropping the most favourable section; otherwise no_change.
The test never changes a live budget, score, action or size. A promotion_candidate only earns a replay challenger evaluated through the promotion test.

items.title: Hard vs soft news tracked as a trial signal
items.headline: Press releases are sorted into number-based news and story-based news, and stocks are scored on how each moved the price. It's tracked only and affects no recommendations.
items.summary: A new universe SHADOW component news_hardness (±100, Evidence.SHADOW, weight 0.0) in decision_components/universe/news_hardness.py
added: The universe surface SHALL carry a SHADOW component news_hardness (budget ±100, weight 0.0, stocks only) that is recorded on every audit row in shadow_component_scores and never enters composite_10000, an action or a position size.

Each MFN press release in the silver news_events table (Oslo Newsweb rows are excluded) SHALL be classified by fixed title/tag rules as hard (quantified news), soft (story news) or other; other releases are ignored.

A release counts when its reaction session (the same Stockholm day before 17:30, else the next session) is on or before the scoring date, fewer than 20 sessions have passed since that session, and the stock's return that session minus the batch's equal-weight mean is at least 1% in absolute value. Releases sharing a ticker and reaction session count once, as hard if any of them is hard.

The score SHALL be round(100 × tanh(S / 0.05)), clamped to ±100, where S sums each counted event's abnormal day-0 return signed +1 for hard and −1 for soft news. A ticker with no counted event reports insufficient_data:news_hardness.

items.title: Weekly scorecard check allows for Monday timing
items.headline: On Monday mornings, last week's scorecard now counts as present until the new week's first update has run, avoiding false alarms.
items.summary: audit_log.product_health.weekly_decision_scorecard_present takes an optional now
added: t5_weekly_scorecard_present reads MET when the decision scorecard for the most recently completed ISO week exists. On Monday before 12:00 UTC, before the first pulse run of the new week has backfilled that scorecard, the previous completed week's scorecard also satisfies the metric. From 12:00 UTC on Monday, and on every other day, only the most recently completed week counts, so a Monday pulse that fails to write the scorecard still reads MISS the same day.

items.title: Hit rate compared against random buying
items.headline: Each confidence level's success rate is now compared with what random buying across the whole universe on the same dates would have achieved, showing real advantage.
items.summary: Redefine T12 as lift over a date-matched universe random-entry null on the existing cohort-matched, ticker-clustered fixed-horizon basis
added: The cohort-matched, ticker-clustered T12 basis SHALL report, for each conviction band and entry cohort, a universe random-entry null: the hit rate and mean 13-week return of buying every investable-universe ticker on each date the band recorded a decision, resolved on the same fixed-horizon rule and weighted to the band's date mix with each band ticker counted once (the same clustering as the band). It SHALL also report the band's lift over that null in hit rate (percentage points) and in mean 13-week return.

items.title: Skipped weekly strategy review is carried forward
items.headline: If the weekly strategy review is skipped, the next available automated run now does it instead of waiting another week.
items.summary: strategy_slot_due() returns True at the slot itself, or when the audit log has no strategy-mode engineer row since the most recent Sunday 14:00
added: The weekly strategy obligation carries forward. If no strategy-mode engineer run has been recorded since the most recent Sunday 14:00 slot start, the next engineer run that clears the usage window-guard runs in strategy mode. A run skipped by the window-guard does not discharge the obligation. The manual force override still takes precedence. If the audit log is unreadable, only the plain Sunday-slot match applies.

items.title: Cleaner labels on archived change records
items.headline: Archived changes are now tagged only with the goals they actually affect, instead of picking up goals mentioned in a denial.
items.summary: Four archive commits on 2026-10-12 had wrong subjects (persona-panel-composite-scale, panel-holding-scope, holdings-fundamentals-market-ticker, holdings-ratio-cache).
added: An archive commit subject's target list includes only targets the proposal's Product contribution section claims to move. A sentence that names a target range under a negation, such as "No risk invariant (T1–T4) changes.", contributes no targets. A positive range ("Moves T6–T8") still does.
The subject's impact text is the first paragraph of Product contribution. Tables and evidence paragraphs are excluded.

items.title: Fewer false warnings about new health measures
items.headline: The automated check no longer mistakes a mention of an existing health measure for adding a new one.
items.summary: openspec_gate check warned "Proposal appears to add a health metric" on two proposals in the 2026-10-12 run (holdings-fundamentals-market-ticker, holdings-ratio-cache)
added: The metric-budget check does not treat a reference to an existing health metric as adding one. Existing metrics are every t<n>_… name defined by a Metric, plus every metric name defined in the product-health module, including unprefixed names such as portfolio_conviction_score. Both "the health metric <existing name>" and "the health metric moves/updates/reflects" are references. A health-metric phrase that names an undefined metric still warns.

items.title: Valuation ratios for foreign-currency holdings
items.headline: Stocks you hold that trade in other currencies now show price-to-earnings, price-to-book, dividend yield and growth figures instead of missing data.
items.summary: fetch_fundamentals trips on any non-SEK quote currency, because the universe cache is SEK-only by spec
added: Held stocks that the SEK-only fundamentals cache does not cover (non-SEK quote currency) get unit-free ratios in a separate holdings-only cache, data/holding_ratios_cache.json. The ratios are P/E, P/B, trailing dividend yield, revenue growth and earnings growth, with the quote currency recorded. No absolute, currency-denominated figure is stored, and the decision engine and the universe cache never read it. The SEK-only rule for the universe is unchanged.
The pulse refreshes rows that are missing or older than 7 days, for held market-data symbols absent from the fundamentals cache. A failed fetch keeps the old row and never aborts the pulse.

A stock holding's fundamentals lookup order is: 1. the fundamentals cache under the exact market-data symbol; 2. the holdings ratio cache under that symbol; 3. the broker ticker (± .ST) in the fundamentals cache.

items.title: Holdings matched to the right company data
items.headline: Some of your holdings were wrongly shown as lacking data because of ticker naming differences. Their valuation and growth figures now appear.
items.summary: The holdings-surface valuation and growth components look up data/fundamentals_cache.json by the holding's broker ticker (± .ST)
added: A stock holding's valuation and growth components read the fundamentals snapshot stored under the holding's verified market-data symbol (HoldingsRegistry.market_data_ticker_for) first, then under its own ticker (± .ST). A holding whose broker ticker differs from the provider symbol (HUFD-A → HUFV-A.ST, FABE → FABG.ST, STENHU → SFAST.ST, FLAT-C → FLAT-B.ST) is not reported as insufficient_data while its fundamentals are cached.

items.title: Expert panel no longer rejects holdings as off-universe
items.headline: The review panel stops objecting that a stock you already own is outside the screened universe, and judges instead whether to keep holding it.
items.summary: The expert-panel prompt opens "for a Swedish small/midcap equity screener"
added: The expert-panel prompt treats universe membership, market cap and listing venue as decided upstream. They are not risks for the panel to judge.

When the panel evaluates a held position that the screening universe does not cover, its prompt labels the name as an existing personal holding outside the universe, to be judged on whether to keep holding it. Names in the universe carry no scope label. Their panel-cache input is unchanged, so the change does not force a full panel re-run.

items.title: Review panels now see the correct score scale
items.headline: The review panels were shown the overall score on the wrong scale, which could skew their vetoes. They now see the true scale, and results are version-tagged.
items.summary: The expert-panel prompt prints Composite score: {composite_score}/100, and the adversarial-persona prompt prints {composite_score}/100
added: Every LLM prompt that shows the engine composite (the expert panel and the adversarial personas) states the composite's real scale: signed, -10000..+10000, 0 = neutral. A prompt never labels the composite with a different denominator (for example "/100"). A mislabelled scale is an input error, and the panel must not be able to veto on it.

The expert panel and persona prompt versions are bumped whenever an input's stated meaning changes. Each persisted panel and persona result records the version it was produced under, so a reader can split results produced before and after the correction (T5).

items.title: Fewer false alarms about slow daily steps
items.headline: Steps that usually finish instantly are now flagged as slow only after taking over a minute, rather than after a few seconds.
items.summary: Raise a stage's median to the 30s floor before applying the 2× factor: a stage is flagged when its latest duration exceeds 2 × max(median, 30s)
added: In Pulse slow stages, a stage's median below 30 seconds is raised to 30 seconds before the 2× comparison, so a stage that is usually a no-op is flagged only when its latest duration exceeds 60 seconds. Stages with a median of 30 seconds or more are judged against 2× their own median.

items.title: Monitoring ignores harmless missing-data messages
items.headline: Routine messages about a stock having no price data from the data source no longer count as errors in the system monitoring.
items.summary: One shared predicate, log_sentinel.is_benign_error_line, recognises a yfinance per-ticker data-miss line: a [yfinance] line whose text is empty, says possibly delisted, or is an HTTP Error 404
added: The log sentinel and the healer's journal scan do not count an error-level line that records an expected per-ticker data miss from yfinance (a possibly delisted line, a quote-API HTTP Error 404, or yfinance's blank continuation line). Other yfinance errors, including rate limits, and all other error lines still count.

items.title: Research into funding strength reopened
items.headline: Research into which companies can keep funding themselves is restarted. Eligible companies and rules are fixed in advance, before any results are examined.
items.summary: Reopen the research line as a new change and execute the findings' order, one step per task, with no outcome inspected before step 4 is frozen.
added: Funding Resilience research is reopened. The 2026-10-10 coverage preflight returned 166 point-in-time candidates across 72 issuers, above the pre-registered floor of 100.

Before any annotation, extractor tuning or outcome inspection, the research MUST freeze a versioned, digested sector-eligibility rule set and funding-fact schema, and write a cohort freeze artifact listing every candidate with its route and exclusion reason, plus the eligibility, schema and corpus digests.

Eligibility routes are industrial, property (same rubric, reported as a separate stratum), ineligible_financial (banks, brokers, credit managers, insurers, investment companies) and ineligible_unclassified (no sector label and no override). Frozen ticker lists take precedence over the universe sector label. A "Utilities" label is not an exclusion.
A candidate report is excluded as the wrong document when it was published on or before the end of its labelled fiscal year, or when its text body is under 150,000 characters.
